name: Hodaviah
overview: Hodaviah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Hassenuah. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused primarily on his genealogical placement within the Benjaminite lineage. There are no additional notes or distinguishing events recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodaviah means 'give thanks to YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning that honors the Lord. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant spiritual gratitude in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hodaviah as the son of Hassenuah. It is also inferred that Meshuallam was his father, establishing a familial line within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Though Hodaviah appears only briefly in the biblical record, his inclusion in the genealogical listings underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving the lineage of Benjamin. His name, meaning 'give thanks to YHWH,' serves as a reminder of the importance of gratitude toward God within the covenant community. Hodaviah’s mention contributes to the broader biblical narrative that values heritage and the continuity of God's people.
